newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 28.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:
* In recent years, 20 states have imposed term limits on their state legislators, prompting a high lawmaker turnover.

* President Clinton joined former U.S. presidents George Bush and Jimmy Carter and General Colin Powell to clean up graffiti and trash in Philadelphia, and to set a national example to encourage volunteerism.
* The cautious election campaign of Britain's Labour leader Tony Blair has shed less light on his plans for the country than it has on him.

* Bonnie Lu Trusdale Nettles and Marshall Herff Applewhite, the Heaven's Gate cult leaders who died in the recent mass suicide in California, went from having strong religious zeal to believing in what seemed a bleak and delusional doctrine.
* Los Angeles remains divided about the progress of efforts to bring new jobs to its inner cities, five years after riots broke out there.

* The murder of Robert Wardlow Jr, a young black man in the South Bend, Indiana area, has caused families and politicians to work out racial tensions as the trial nears. Police say Wardlow Jr was killed at random in retaliation for the slaying of a white 17-year-old girl.

* A Vietnamese journalist who covered the war for Time magazine while also serving as a colonel in the North Vietnam Army was denied an exit visa by that government to come to New York to discuss the war's legacy.
